title: WH-cleft ／ Pseudo-cleft

omissions: Every numbered Important Rule and Benefit is retained as a separate Chinese-primary card. Where the PDF has no complete English counterpart, the English explanation is a faithful editorial translation.

example: What the team lacked was trust.
exampleZh: 團隊所缺乏的，就是信任。

examples.en: What the team lacked was trust.
examples.zh: 團隊所缺乏的，就是信任。
examples.highlight: What the team lacked was trust.

meaning.zh: WH 分裂句把一個意思分成 WH 子句和焦點資料兩部分，讓說話者突出最重要的內容。

rules.zh: 子句使用陳述句語序 WH-cleft 中的 WH 部分並不是直接問句，因此不能使用問句語序。 Correct: What he needs is more time. （他所需要的是更多時間。） Incorrect: What does he need is more time.
rules.en: Use statement word order in the WH-clause because it is not a direct question: “What he needs is more time”, not “What does he need ...”.

rules.zh: 根據所強調的資料選擇 WH 疑問詞 What I need is some rest. （我所需要的是休息。） Where we met was outside the station. （我們見面的地方是在車站外。） When the problem began was last Monday. （問題開始的時間是上星期一。） Why she resigned was that she felt ignored. （她辭職的原因是她感到不受重視。） How they succeeded was by working together. （他們成功的方法是共同合作。） Who helped us most was Daniel. （最幫到我們的人是丹尼爾。） Which option we selected was the cheaper one. （我們所選擇的是較便宜的選項。）
rules.en: Choose the WH-word according to the focus: what for a thing or idea, where for place, when for time, why for reason, how for method, who for a person, and which for a choice.

rules.zh: 一般根據時間使用 is 或 was What I need now is more information. （我現在所需要的是更多資料。） What surprised me yesterday was his answer. （昨天令我驚訝的是他的答案。）
rules.en: Choose is or was according to the relevant time: “What I need now is ...” but “What surprised me yesterday was ....”

rules.zh: 子句放在前面時，通常視作一個整體 因此，標準 WH-cleft 通常使用 is 或 was。 What the students need is more practice. （學生所需要的是更多練習。）
rules.en: When the WH-clause comes first, it is normally treated as a single unit, so a standard WH-cleft usually uses is or was.

rules.zh: 倒置偽分裂句的 be 動詞可與前面的重點配合 A clearer explanation is what the students need. （學生所需要的是更清晰的解釋。） Clearer signs were what made the building easier to navigate. （令大樓更容易找到方向的是更清晰的指示牌。）
rules.en: In a reversed pseudo-cleft, the form of be can agree with the preceding focused information and its time.

rules.zh: 後面常使用原形動詞 What we should do is check the figures again. （我們應該做的是再次核對數字。） What the doctor advised me to do was get more rest. （醫生建議我做的是多休息。）
rules.en: After “What ... do is/was”, the focused action commonly uses the base verb: “What we should do is check the figures again.”

rules.zh: 子句後宜使用 that 子句表達原因 Why the meeting was cancelled was that the speaker was ill. （會議取消的原因是講者生病了。） 這種寫法通常比以下形式更清晰： Why the meeting was cancelled was because the speaker was ill.
rules.en: After a why-clause, a that-clause often expresses the reason more clearly than a because-clause.

rules.zh: 並非所有倒置形式都同樣自然 以下句子自然： Trust was what the team lacked. Friday evening was when the event began. Checking every figure twice was how Ben avoided mistakes. 但以下句子較生硬： Daniel was who helped me most. 因此，who 和 which 類句子通常保留 WH 子句在前面的形式，以確保英語自然。
rules.en: Not every reversed form is equally natural. Reversed what, where, when, why and how forms are common, but who and which often sound more natural with the WH-clause first.

benefits.zh: 把最重要的資料放在焦點位置 這個句型可以清楚告訴聽者或讀者，句子中哪一部分最重要。 The team lacked trust. What the team lacked was trust. 第二句把 trust 放在最受注意的位置。
benefits.en: It places the most important information in a clear focus position.

benefits.zh: 適合澄清或更正資料 當你想強調「真正重要的不是 X，而是 Y」時，WH-cleft 十分實用。 What we need is better communication, not another meeting. （我們所需要的是更好的溝通，而不是再開一次會議。）
benefits.en: It is useful for correcting or clarifying information by contrasting the real focus with an alternative.

benefits.zh: 幫助組織較複雜的解釋 你可以利用 what、where、when、why 和 how，把內容分成清楚的類別。 ● what happened：發生了甚麼； ● where it happened：在哪裏發生； ● when it happened：何時發生； ● why it happened：為甚麼發生； ● how it happened：如何發生。 這能令說明、報告和故事更容易理解。
benefits.en: It helps organise complex explanations by grouping information under what, where, when, why and how.

benefits.zh: 增加句子開頭的變化 你不需要每一句都以人物或事物作主語。 普通句： The lack of trust caused the problem. WH-cleft： What caused the problem was the lack of trust. 倒置偽分裂句： The lack of trust was what caused the problem. 三句表達相近意思，但句子的組織方式不同。
benefits.en: It creates more varied sentence openings instead of beginning every sentence with a person or thing.

benefits.zh: 令說話更有條理 WH-cleft 可以成為一個容易使用的口語框架： What I think is... What concerns me is... What we should do is... Why this matters is... How we can improve is... 掌握這些框架後，你可以更快組織答案，不需要每次從零開始構思整句。
benefits.en: It gives spoken answers an organised framework, such as “What I think is ...” or “How we can improve is ....”
